title: Observability ingress gateway for Dedicated & Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Problem: Dedicated and Private deployments currently rely on ad-hoc collectors and cross-tenant egress patterns that complicate tenant isolation, mTLS setup, and per-customer sampling/retention policies. Goal: Implement a unified Observability Ingress Gateway that sits at the customer boundary for Dedicated and VPC/on‑prem installs. The gateway will authenticate tenant tokens, terminate mTLS when applicable, apply per-tenant ingress policies (sampling, rate limits, retention tags), buffer and batch telemetry for variable connectivity in on‑prem environments, and forward to segregated backend pipelines for traces, metrics, and logs. This ticket covers design, implementation plan, acceptance criteria, and rollout strategy for the gateway MVP that supports multi‑tenant logical separation without requiring changes to existing customers' telemetry SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress Gateway deployed in a Dedicated environment and an on‑prem lab; accepts traces, metrics, and logs over OTLP and HTTPS
Gateway validates per-tenant signed JWTs or client certs and associates tenant_id to all incoming telemetry
Per-tenant sampling and rate limiting rules are configurable via the Console and enforced by the gateway
Telemetry for each tenant is forwarded to isolated backend pipelines (logical partitions) without data leakage across tenants
Gateway provides durability: local disk-backed buffering for intermittent on‑prem connectivity and at-least-once delivery to backend
End-to-end latency and error dashboards in Console show gateway ingress metrics, and SLO dashboards can be scoped per tenant
Automated tests cover auth failure paths, high-throughput scenarios, and tenant partitioning correctness
Security review completed and documented; key material (TLS keys, JWT signing keys) can be integrated with customer KMS/HSM in Private deployments
implementation_notes: Protocol support: OTLP/gRPC for traces/metrics, HTTPS (JSON/NDJSON) for logs, and a lightweight HTTP health endpoint
Auth: prefer mTLS for Dedicated-managed agents; support signed tenant JWTs as a fallback for third-party SDKs and on‑prem agents
Tenant binding: gateway attaches standardized headers (x-rw-tenant-id, x-rw-trace-source) and enforces SRP mapping for routing to backend tenants
Sampling engine: pluggable sampling module (head-based and tail-based) with per-tenant policy store backed by Console config service
Rate limiting: token-bucket per-tenant with burst allowances tied to customer tier; soft-deny vs hard-drop modes configurable
Buffering: write-ahead queue on local disk with configurable retention TTL and backpressure signals to producers (429 when queue exhausted)
Encryption: in-transit TLS for all upstream connections; at-rest encryption for local buffers using node-level keys or customer KMS
Observability: gateway emits internal metrics (ingest_rps, ingest_errors, buffer_size, auth_failures) and structured logs with tenant_id
Routing: logical partitioning implemented via tenant_id header and separate Kafka topics/S3 prefixes in backend to avoid co-mingling
Operational hooks: admin API for draining, toggling per-tenant rules, and rotating certs without gateway restarts
decisions: Choose a dedicated ingress gateway process instead of embedding in existing collectors to simplify lifecycle and updates across deployments
Use signed tenant JWTs as a cross-environment fallback to support legacy integrations and third-party telemetry SDKs
Implement per-tenant logical partitioning at the queue/topic level (backend) rather than multi-instance gateway per tenant to reduce resource footprint
Expose sampling and rate-limit configs in Console but keep enforcement in gateway to minimize control-plane latency
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Implement MVP in staging cluster, enable for internal customers and infra teams only
Stage 2: Smoke tests + synthetic high-throughput load tests (100k req/s combined telemetry) in Dedicated dev cluster
Stage 3: Canary: enable gateway for 5 low-risk Dedicated customers; monitor ingress metrics and per-tenant dashboards for 72h
Stage 4: Private onboarding: provide an opt-in helm chart for on‑prem customers with additional docs for KMS integration and cert provisioning
Stage 5: Gradual ramp to all Dedicated clusters and update default ingestion instructions for new customers
Rollback: gateway supports canary weight and immediate disable per-customer rules; have script to revert routing to legacy collectors
test_plan: Unit tests for tenant auth, policy evaluation, and sampling logic
Integration tests: OTLP/gRPC ingest -> gateway -> backend pipeline with tenant separation verification
Load tests: 100k rps combined with mixed traces/metrics/logs, verify backpressure behavior and latency SLOs
Chaos tests: simulate backend outage and verify local buffering durability and delivery semantics
Security tests: cert rotation, JWT replay protection, and privilege escalation checks
Penetration test for on-prem helm chart and gateway admin API

2026-02-18 Markus Nguyen: Architecture looks good. Suggest using packet-level TLS termination only for Dedicated; for on-prem allow both mTLS and JWT to reduce ops burden for customers.
2026-02-20 Product (Lena Ortiz): Product acceptance: per-tenant retention and sampling must be surfaced in Console; need UX story for 'ingest policy' page. Adding follow-up PM ticket.
2026-02-27 Security (Noah Park): Reviewed threat model; require JTI (nonce) in tenant JWTs and 1h max TTL. Also require admin API protected by RBAC and IAM integration.
2026-03-01 Eng (Jing Wei): Implemented auth middleware prototype. PR: https://github.com/redwood/ingress-gateway/pull/1234. Observability metrics added to staging. Performance looks promising.
2026-03-04 QA (Ravi Patel): Load test results attached in Drive; gateway sustained 80k rps with 99th pct latency 85ms. Observability dashboards created at /console/observability/ingress-gateway
